rows.grounds: compound adjective describing the locus of the practice; lalāṭa (forehead) + varṇa (syllable/letter) + rāśi (mass) + stha (situated)
object indicating the quantity of repetitions to be performed
absolutive expressing completion of the prescribed act
vocative address to the recipient; sura (god) + arcita (worshipped)

items.question: What quantified practice situated in the forehead’s syllable-mass is required of the one worshipped by the gods?
premises: One hundred thousand repetitions must be performed.
The repetitions are situated in the mass of syllables on the forehead.
The instruction is addressed to one worshipped by the gods.
items.inference: A specific, quantified forehead-centered practice is enjoined upon the worthy, god-worshipped recipient.
uncertainties: The exact nature of the act counted as a 'lakṣa' (e.g., japa or another ritual action) is implied rather than explicitly stated.
items.plain_english: O you who are worshipped by the gods, having performed one hundred thousand repetitions situated in the mass of syllables on the forehead...
